turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ms. Hale, grab a seat. What are we dealing with?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I've been really tired, and my periods are heavy. I don't know, doctor, it's just been a lot.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long have the periods been heavy?
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A year. She burns through pads, I've watched her...
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Jen, let me... well, I don't know if it's a full year. A year sounds right, I guess.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the tiredness?
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Months. She sits down halfway up the stairs at my place.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not sit halfway. I get a little winded at the top, that's it, and that hasn't been going on for months.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did the shortness of breath actually start?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Maybe six weeks? It's just at the top of the stairs.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It was around Christmas. Three months.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): So six weeks from you, three months from your sister. I'm not settling it. Chest pain with it?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cough? Wheeze?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh-uh. No cough, no wheeze.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any dizziness?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't get dizzy.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You said the room spins when you stand up too fast.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): That's not... okay, sometimes if I get up quick everything goes gray for a second. I don't know if that's dizzy, doctor.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hair coming out?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, in the shower, like clumps. A couple months, I think. I don't know exactly when it started.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Heavy day, how many pads?
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh, and tell her about the couch we...
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Jen, not the couch. I don't know, doctor. Six, maybe eight. I lose count. And at night I double them and still...
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Clots?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Bigger than a quarter, sometimes. Not every single day. They just look big, I don't know.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bleeding between periods?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain with sex?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I'm not pregnant either. Copper IUD, they put it in two years ago.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Medication allergies?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None that I know of.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): You on iron?
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She bought the big bottle. It mostly sits on the counter.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): I take it sometimes. Ferrous sulfate, the three twenty-five, I think. It hurts my stomach so I skip it.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many days a week, really?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Maybe three days a week?
[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mom has hypothyroidism, she's on levothyroxine. Aunt Linda had a goiter too, I think.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't have a thyroid thing. You're talking like I do. And Aunt Linda, I don't even know what she had.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Feeling cold? Weight up or down? Constipation?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Cold, yes. Weight's about the same. No constipation.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Work's been crazy, we're short at the library, but that's a whole other thing. Sorry.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Still full time there?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. And I don't smoke. Never have. You were gonna ask.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Heart's regular, rate eighty-eight. Lungs clear. Conjunctiva looks a little pale. No ankle swelling.

[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not calling this anemia today, and I'm not diagnosing a thyroid problem because your mother has one. Could be iron loss from the bleeding, could be thyroid, could be both. I won't pick until the labs are back.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. So what do I... what are we doing?

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood count, ferritin, and TSH today. If the bleeding stays this heavy I'll get a pelvic ultrasound, not right now. Keep the ferrous sulfate, three twenty-five by mouth, but every day, with food. See me in two weeks for the results. Soak a pad an hour or get chest pain, go to the ER, don't wait.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
